questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Equation of a Wide Ellipse
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070132/assets/9eb144bd4109846f3e1af4fb7d8ed70d2d8a29c3804547b89238d6437c4258d8.png)

What is the equation of the ellipse given above?
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the horizontal radius has length $a=3$ and the vertical radius has length $b=1.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{1}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{1} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Lengths of the Major and Minor Axes Given the Equation of an Ellipse
questions.problem:
For the ellipse 
$\frac{{x}^{2}}{64}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{81}=1,$ find the lengths of its major and minor axes.

$\,$ The length of the major axis is 
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ The length of the minor axis is 
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

In the given equation, we have ${a}^{2}=64$ and ${b}^{2}=81.$

- Since ${a}^{2}=64,$ the length of the horizontal radius must be $a=\sqrt{64}=8.$

- Since ${b}^{2}=81,$ the length of the vertical radius must be $b=\sqrt{81}=9.$

Thus, the semi-major axis has length $b=9,$ and the semi-minor axis has length $a=8.$

Therefore, the major axis has length $2b=2\cdot 9=18,$ and the minor axis has length $2a=2\cdot 8=16.$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Lengths of the Major and Minor Axes Given the Equation of an Ellipse
questions.problem:
For the ellipse $\frac{{x}^{2}}{12}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{49}=1,$ find the lengths of its major and minor axes.

$\,$ The length of the major axis is 
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ The length of the minor axis is 
{{field-2}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

In the given equation, we have ${a}^{2}=12$ and ${b}^{2}=49.$

- Since ${a}^{2}=12,$ the length of the horizontal radius must be $a=\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt{3}.$

- Since ${b}^{2}=49,$ the length of the vertical radius must be $b=\sqrt{49}=7.$

Thus, the semi-major axis has length $b=7,$ and the semi-minor axis has length $a=2\sqrt{3}.$

Therefore, the major axis has length $2b=2\cdot 7=14,$ and the minor axis has length $2a=2\cdot 2\sqrt{3}=4\sqrt{3}.$
